title.narrative: Sustainable Water Harvesting for Al-Husseiniya: Enhancing Ecosystem Resilience

description.narrative: The "Sustainable Water Harvesting for Al-Husseiniya: Enhancing Ecosystem Resilience" project aims to tackle water challenges and enhance climate change resilience of the Al-Husseiniya district in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan. By installing rainwater harvesting systems such as hafirsI1, the project will promote sustainable water management practices and enhance resilience to climate change. To conserve and protect local water sources and increase water availability from non-conventional and sustainable water sources within the Hasa minor basin and Al-Husseiniya district, UN-Habitat will collaborate with key stakeholders from Jordan, including government ministries, municipalities, and water establishments. The project will focus on two specific outcomes: (1) increased use of nature-based water harvesting systems and (2) strengthened capacities of local authorities and local communities on sustainable water management practices in Al-Husseiniya district. While its direct beneficiaries include local farmers and communities in Al-Husseiniya district in Jordan, the indirect beneficiaries involve the broader population in the target governorate from improved water resilience. The project outputs comprise the identification of the most flood-vulnerable and hot spot areas that can be utilized for water catchment by conducting spatial analysis and mapping of most flood-vulnerable areas and community consultations and the establishment of a Local Community Committee to increase their awareness and involvement related to water harvesting practices and their effect on volumetric water benefits. Such rainwater harvesting techniques will deliver significant volumetric water benefits and increase water resource availability. Hence, the project focuses on providing access to nature-based water harvesting system and improving the sustainable water management practices in the district with a multi-faceted approach. The project not only aligns with several Sustainable Development Goals, contributing to clean water and sanitation (SDG 6), industry, innovation, and infrastructure (SDG 9), sustainable cities and communities (SDG 11), and climate action (SDG 13), but also with Jordan's Green Growth Action Plan and the National Adaptation Plan. By implementing sustainable water collection and management solutions and engaging the local farmers and communities, the project will create a long-term impact of promoting environmental stewardship and building resilient communities in the face of climate change challenges, bringing about positive change in the lives of the residents in Al-Husseiniya area.
